overview: This Senate resolution names May 2026 "National Wildfire Preparedness Month." It describes wildfires growing larger and fire seasons getting longer, notes that most wildland fires are caused by people, and points to the health risks of smoke for firefighters and the public. It encourages governments at every level, including tribal, Alaska Native and Native Hawaiian communities, along with nonprofits and neighborhoods, to prepare for wildfires. It supports education on steps such as fire-resistant building, clearing flammable brush, early warning systems and safe evacuation for people and pets. It does not create any program or spend any money. As of June 24, 2026, the Senate had approved it.
for: Supporters say raising awareness of practical steps like home hardening and evacuation planning can save lives and property as wildfire risk spreads to new areas.
against: Critics say it is symbolic, was approved after the month had passed, and does not change any law or provide funding for wildfire prevention.
